---
title: "Comparing 90% and 95% Confidence Intervals"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
set.seed(123)
```

# Confidence Interval Comparison

We simulate a sample from a normal distribution and compute both the **90%** and **95%** confidence intervals for the mean.
Then we show them graphically.

```{r}
# Sample data
x <- rnorm(50, mean = 10, sd = 2)

# Estimate
xbar <- mean(x)
s <- sd(x)
n <- length(x)

# Confidence levels
alpha90 <- 0.10
alpha95 <- 0.05

# Critical values (using t distribution)
t90 <- qt(1 - alpha90/2, df = n-1)  # qt(0.95, n-1) 
t95 <- qt(1 - alpha95/2, df = n-1)  # qt(0.975, n-1)

# Confidence intervals
ci90 <- c(xbar - t90*s/sqrt(n), xbar + t90*s/sqrt(n))
ci95 <- c(xbar - t95*s/sqrt(n), xbar + t95*s/sqrt(n))

ci90
ci95
```

# **Graphic: 90% vs 95% Confidence Intervals**

```{r}
# Plot setup
plot(1, xbar, pch = 19, xlim = c(0.5, 1.5), ylim = range(ci95),
     xaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "Value",
     main = "Comparison of Confidence Interval Widths\n(Base R Graphics)")

axis(1, at = 1, labels = FALSE)

# Draw 95% CI (wider)
segments(1, ci95[1], 1, ci95[2], lwd = 6, col = "skyblue")
points(1, xbar, pch = 19, col = "blue")

# Draw 90% CI (narrower), slightly shifted for visibility
segments(1.05, ci90[1], 1.05, ci90[2], lwd = 6, col = "orange")
points(1.05, xbar, pch = 19, col = "red")

# Legend
legend("topright",
       legend = c("95% CI (wider)", "90% CI (narrower)"),
       col = c("skyblue", "orange"),
       lwd = 6,
       bty = "n")
```
